surprises_or_findings:
1. The dual-signal model is a textbook architectural disambiguation. Both PRECOND_WAVE_BEADS_EXIST and PRECOND_WAVE_BEADS_OF_ANY_STATUS_EXIST share the refusalCode=NO_WAVE_BEADS but use different signals (openWaveBeadIds vs anyStatusWaveBeadIds). The failedCheck field disambiguates them ('wave-beads-exist' vs 'wave-beads-of-any-status-exist'). This is the right shape per ADR-001's discriminated-union design — operators can grep by failedCheck for site-specific debugging while the high-level refusalCode remains stable for downstream filtering.

2. The 1cb58a5-success-case lock-in test (`PRECOND_WAVE_BEADS_OF_ANY_STATUS_EXIST.evaluate(ctx({ action: 'review-wave', anyStatusWaveBeadIds: ['closed-bead-1', 'closed-bead-2'], openWaveBeadIds: [] })) → ok=true`) is a strong example of POSITIVE regression-testing. It explicitly locks in the success case the original 1cb58a5 fix enabled — so any future ACTIONS_REQUIRING_WAVE_BEADS edit that re-couples review-wave to openWaveBeadIds will fail this test first. This addresses Round 1's finding that 1cb58a5 added zero new tests for new behaviour.

3. The o2s amendment is a clean example of marker-discipline correction. The original ehp.10 marker silently misclassified the deviation; Round 1 caught it; 5c9e058 amends only the marker text (no code) and explicitly documents the failure mode (Out clause infeasible against existing kvn tests), the alternative considered (STOP-and-Surface), and the chosen disposition (ACCEPT). This is exactly what marker-protocol § 2 'Flag inconsistencies with prior work' is for — and the second-line-defense (reviewer) caught it the first time.

4. The pre-existing already-tracked open bugs (poh.1 framework-exits, poh.3 hardcoded path, poh.4 reconciler tick contention) are correctly NOT re-filed in Round 2. They are infrastructure / cross-cutting concerns that pre-date or post-date Wave 4 and overlap with the review window. This matches Round 1's interpretation: 'any open bug means FAIL' applies to bugs FILED BY this review against this wave's work, not to pre-existing infrastructure backlog.

5. The route.ts:496 hardcoded path remains unfixed at HEAD (verified by grep). This is poh.3's explicit scope and is not Wave-4-attributable — Round 1 already documented this. Wave 4 review continues to surface it for operator awareness but does not block on it.

6. Reconciler tick contention (poh.4) emerged AFTER the m2c fix landed — likely amplified by ehp.4-9's per-tick buildDispatchContext calls (each call yields BD_READ_FAILED + event write + log line for cross-repo epics; multiplied by 40 repos × 10s tick = thousands of bd subprocess invocations per minute). The 6667571 commit mitigates via 60s throttle; the proper fix (prewarm only active repos, stagger rules, semaphore action POST priority) is tracked under poh.4. This is a legitimate downstream consequence of Wave 4's defense-in-depth fan-out and was not foreseeable from the Wave-4 unit/integration tests — flagged as observability surface for future epic-decomposition rounds.
